program: SNAP — Nebraska has no distinctive local program nickname; DHHS's own consumer pages use plain "SNAP" (formerly Food Stamps), see PROVENANCE.md
agency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
agency_short: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
admin_note: Nebraska is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program (no county option-in like CA/NY/MN/WI/VA) — DHHS administers directly through its Economic Assistance division, with no county-level policy variation. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING this pack found: unlike most of this roster's states, where a single BBCE percentage applies to every household, Nebraska's elevated 165% FPL gross-income column on DHHS's own current SNAP Program Standards table applies ONLY to "Elderly, Disabled, Separate Household, and ERP [Expanded Resource Program] Households" — an ordinary working-age household that has not separately qualified for Nebraska's Expanded Resource Program remains subject to the plain federal 130% FPL gross-income test, not 165%. Nebraska's ERP is also a RESOURCE-limit mechanism (raising the asset ceiling to $25,000, not waiving it outright) rather than the asset-waiver-plus-flat-income-ceiling shape this roster's other BBCE states generally use — see income-pathways supplement. SEPARATE FLAGSHIP FINDING: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 68-1017.02 statutorily bars DHHS from seeking, applying for, accepting, or renewing an AREA-WIDE ABAWD work-requirement waiver except where expressly required by federal law — Nebraska's current lack of any ABAWD waiver is a legislative mandate, not merely a labor-market/policy-choice fact the way it is in most other states this roster has built (see abawd-work-requirement supplement). THIRD FLAGSHIP FINDING: a 2025 bill (LB319) that would have replaced Nebraska's current MODIFIED drug-felony ban with a broader eligibility rule passed the full Legislature 32-17 but was VETOED by Gov. Jim Pillen the same day, and a veto-override motion failed 24-24 (six votes short of the 30 needed) — the pre-existing, narrower Neb. Rev. Stat. § 68-1017.02(1)(b) modified ban remains CURRENT, unchanged law, directly contradicting several secondary sources (and this pack's own initial web-search synthesis) that describe Nebraska as having already "opted out" of the federal drug-felony ban (see criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement). Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DHHS office, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD/CO/SC/AL/LA/KY/OK/CT.
system: DHHS's Economic Assistance division processes SNAP centrally (no county offices with independent policy authority); applicants apply online through iServe Nebraska (iserve.nebraska.gov, DHHS's current self-service portal, successor to the ACCESSNebraska/N-FOCUS branding still visible on some older DHHS materials and forms — see program-identity supplement), by phone through the Economic Assistance Contact Center (1-800-383-4278), by mail, or in person at a local DHHS office. Most non-elderly/disabled households are Simplified Reporting (SR) households; households where every member is elderly (60+) or disabled with no earned income may receive a 12-month certification period without periodic reporting, or a 24-month certification period with a 12-month periodic report — this pack flags this specific detail as lower-confidence, see freshness.json.
